headline_marked: Yandex [[open-sources 80B AliceAI-Foundation model]] trained from scratch, featuring MoE and 262K context
headline: Yandex open-sources 80B AliceAI-Foundation model trained from scratch, featuring MoE and 262K context
summary: This experimental base model boasts an MoE architecture, delivering 80B knowledge with 3B per-token compute and 262K context via Kimi Delta Attention, excelling in Russian-speaking knowledge and math.
details: Yandex has open-sourced AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base, a language model trained entirely from scratch without borrowed weights. Released on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0, it's an experimental base model designed as a testbed for future agentic features in its Alice AI assistant.

Despite being almost 3x smaller overall and 7x smaller in active parameters than Yandex's previous 235B flagship, this 80B model reportedly surpasses it on facts, math, code, and long context. It achieves the knowledge capacity of an 80B model with roughly the per-token compute of a 3B one.

The model's Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture routes every token through 10 of 512 small experts, plus one shared expert that is always active. This design allows for efficient processing while maintaining a large knowledge base.

Another key feature is its attention stack, where three out of every four layers use Kimi Delta Attention. This linear attention variant folds history into a fixed-size state, enabling a 262K context window without the typical KV-cache bloat, crucial for long-document workloads.

Benchmarks reveal strong performance in areas requiring knowledge of the Russian-speaking world, where it outperforms models 4x its active size. It also shows robust math capabilities, scoring 96.9 on HMMT Feb 2026 (pass@32) compared to Qwen3.5's 87.9.

However, on English trivia and general knowledge benchmarks like TriviaQA and MMLU-Pro, larger models like Nemotron and DeepSeek still lead. This indicates that while efficient, 80B parameters cannot store as much global information as models with 284B parameters.

While 3B active parameters suggest laptop-friendly use, the full 80B model requires significant memory, estimated at 160 GB in bf16 or 45 GB at 4-bit. Official recipes currently target NVIDIA GPUs using transformers and vLLM, with KDA layers needing flash-linear-attention kernels.

GGUF or MLX quants were not available on release day, and non-standard attention layers often delay broader compatibility. Nevertheless, this fully in-house model with a permissive license and detailed technical report provides a valuable foundation for developers building Russian-language products, especially in legal, education, and reference applications.

headline_marked: After 8 Years in Space, [[BepiColombo Is Finally Approaching Mercury]]
headline: After 8 Years in Space, BepiColombo Is Finally Approaching Mercury
summary: The joint ESA/JAXA probe, after a propulsion malfunction and a 6-billion-mile journey, has begun its descent to low orbit around Mercury, with full observations set for April 2027.
details: After an eight-year journey and a propulsion malfunction that delayed its arrival by nearly a year, the BepiColombo space probe is finally beginning its descent to low orbit around Mercury. On September 3, ground control confirmed the propulsion module successfully separated, marking the final phase of the joint European Space Agency (ESA) and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) mission.

Reaching Mercury is particularly challenging due to its proximity to the Sun. Spacecraft must expend significant fuel not to travel towards the Sun, but to slow down and avoid falling into its immense gravitational pull. This requires complex maneuvers to control velocity.

BepiColombo has traveled approximately 6 billion miles (9.9 billion kilometers), executing nine gravity assist maneuvers by swinging around Earth once, Venus twice, and Mercury six times. These maneuvers were crucial for controlling its speed and trajectory after the initial propulsion issue.

Once in position, BepiColombo will split into two separate spacecraft: the Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) to study the planet's surface and internal structure, and the Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (Mio) to investigate its magnetic field and tenuous atmosphere. This marks the first time multiple probes will orbit Mercury simultaneously, aiming for a comprehensive picture.

After a series of preparatory procedures, full-scale scientific observations are scheduled to begin in April 2027. The probes will seek answers to key questions, including why Mercury has an unusually large iron core, why ice exists in permanently shadowed craters, why it possesses its own magnetic field, and the nature of mysterious surface depressions known as 'hollows'.

The mission's findings are expected to provide crucial clues about how terrestrial planets, including Earth, formed and evolved within our solar system. Astrophysicists also plan to use precise orbital data from BepiColombo to test Einstein’s general theory of relativity, leveraging Mercury's unique position close to the Sun as an ideal testing ground for gravitational distortion of spacetime.
